look_here_first: ANATHERUM TENUISPATHEUM is an accepted distinct bluestem, old Andropogon glomeratus var. pumilus 'ROBUST VARIANT', NOT the separate accepted Southwestern Anatherum eremicum (= var. scabriglumis). A published Texas-authored key supports typically SMOOTH sheaths, enclosing raceme sheath <2.5 mm, true ligule membrane <1 mm with LONG cilia, sessile spikelet <3.8 mm. Contrast eremicum's scabrous sheaths, >2.5 mm raceme sheath, 1–2 mm membrane with short cilia, >4.2 mm spikelets. The current archived source-labelled flowering photograph lacks a ruler, true ligule and spikelet macro: no ID hold clearance. Compare A. glomeratum and virginicum separately.

field_id_lesson.look_here_first: ANATHERUM TENUISPATHEUM: a third, separately accepted bluestem species. Kew treats old Andropogon glomeratus var. pumilus (and A. tenuispatheus) as synonyms here, NOT under A. glomeratum. Compare a whole mature flowering culm, spathe enclosing each paired raceme, then a mm-scale sessile/pedicellate spikelet pair against true A. glomeratum and A. virginicum; the existing photo alone is insufficient to separate these.
crew_checkpoints: Document the entire flowering culm and where each raceme pair emerges from its spathe.
Measure the spathe and raceme length from a mature specimen; retain actual measurements rather than guessing species-level thresholds.
At 10–20× magnification photograph the rachis joints, paired spikelets, awn insertion and visible hairs with a millimeter reference.
Photograph the leaf collar and ligule, then compare the complete reproductive unit against source-verified specimens.
For tenuispatheum, check generally smooth sheaths, raceme sheaths usually under 2.5 mm wide, a ligule membrane under 1 mm with long marginal hairs, and sessile spikelets usually under 3.8 mm.
The eremicus contrast has rough sheaths, usually wider raceme sheaths, a 1–2 mm membrane with shorter hairs, and sessile spikelets usually over 4.2 mm. Use the combined characters.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — THREE BLUESTEMS, NOT ONE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Silky spathe-enclosed paired racemes are only a starting clue; this species needs measured parts.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Trace a complete mature flowering culm and locate the narrow sheath (spathe) surrounding each flowering raceme pair. This is a separately accepted Anatherum species historically called Andropogon glomeratus var. pumilus, not automatically true bushy bluestem (A. glomeratum). The current Linda Jo Conn image and Starr historical-variety images teach gross habit only. Do not certify the source photo or a Hays occurrence as this species from a fluffy head. Gallery 0 is the sole source-labelled original flowering image; panels 1, 4 and 5 are historical var. pumilus source views, not independent modern vouchers or measured anatomy.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PROVISIONAL — SPECIES ID NOT VERIFIED FROM GROSS PHOTOS

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · TOUCH AND MEASURE THE UPPER SHEATH
field_id_short_tiles.short: Published key: upper sheaths generally smooth; raceme-enclosing sheath often under 2.5 mm wide.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Wipff and Shaw's Texas-authored 2018 key contrasts A. tenuispatheum's mostly smooth upper leaf sheaths and narrow raceme-enclosing sheath, typically less than 2.5 mm wide, with A. eremicum's often scabrous upper sheath and wider, often over 2.5 mm enclosing sheath. Measure a mature attached enclosing sheath perpendicular to its width, with a 1-mm bar; the published tendencies are not absolute cutoffs. No existing photo proves this texture or width.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · FIND THE TRUE MEMBRANOUS LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: True ligule membrane usually under 1 mm with long marginal cilia.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Open the inner blade/sheath collar at 10–20× and measure the actual membranous ligule, not adjacent throat hairs or a folded leaf blade. The published tenuispatheum condition is a membrane less than 1 mm with relatively long marginal cilia; A. eremicum more often has a 1–2 mm membrane with shorter cilia. Both structure and scale must be visible on the same authenticated specimen. Existing habit photos cannot demonstrate either condition.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PUBLISHED MEASUREMENT — TRUE COLLAR MACRO MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · SESSILE SPIKELET, GLUMES, LEMMA AND AWN
field_id_short_tiles.short: Published key: mature sessile spikelet usually under 3.8 mm; eremicum often over 4.2 mm.
field_id_short_tiles.details: At 10–20× photograph one intact sessile/pedicellate spikelet pair still attached to a raceme joint with a 1-mm ruler. Identify the sessile fertile spikelet separately from its pedicellate partner, then expose the outer glumes and fertile lemma/palea to trace any awn to its true point of origin. Wipff and Shaw contrast a typically <3.8 mm sessile spikelet here with >4.2 mm in A. eremicum; overlapping or damaged material must remain undetermined. No independent glume, lemma, or awn dimensions are certified from the current photographs.
field_id_short_tiles.status: MEASURED SPIKELET KEY — SAME-VOUCHER DISSECTION MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · CENTRAL TEXAS LOOK-ALIKES AND NAME TRAP
field_id_short_tiles.short: Separate bushy bluestem, broomsedge and southwestern A. eremicum.
field_id_short_tiles.details: A. glomeratum generally has a dense brushlike terminal crown of many short silky racemes; A. virginicum more often has separated spathe-enclosed units. Neither gross pattern alone proves A. tenuispatheum. The especially important southwest comparison is separately accepted A. eremicum: use upper-sheath texture, enclosing-sheath width, true ligule and sessile spikelet together. Historical 'var. pumilus' photo labels and synonym spelling differences do not substitute for a modern voucher. Keep county-range status unchanged. For side-by-side gross habit, gallery 0 is the provisional target and galleries 2 (A. virginicum) and 3 (A. glomeratum) are explicitly DIFFERENT species; no authenticated A. eremicum photo is installed.
